akhfash:6-6.t: He said ﴿فَقَالُوۤاْ أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنَا﴾: He used the plural because "البَشَر" (human being) is in meaning a group.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾, i.e. declares Him transcendent; so the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and مَا is used rather than مَنْ, giving predominance (taghlīb) to the majority. ﴿لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ فَمِنْكُمْ كَافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ in the origin of creation; then He causes you to die and brings you back upon that. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ﴾, since He made the form of the human being the best of forms; ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ﴾ of what is in them of secrets and beliefs.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ﴾, O disbelievers of Mecca, ﴿نَبَأُ﴾ the news ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ فَذَاقُوا وَبَالَ أَمْرِهِمْ﴾ the punishment for disbelief in this world, ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful?

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾, i.e. the punishment of this world, ﴿بِأَنَّهُ﴾ — the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) — ﴿كَانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ the manifest proofs for faith, ﴿فَقَالُوا أَبَشَرٌ﴾ — the genus is meant by it — ﴿يَهْدُونَنَا فَكَفَرُوا وَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ from faith, ﴿وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ﴾ of their faith; ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ﴾ independent of His creation, ﴿حَمِيدٌ﴾ praised in His acts.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ﴾: lightened (from anna), its ism omitted, i.e. "that they" ﴿لَنْ يُبْعَثُوا قُلْ بَلَى وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِمَا عَمِلْتُمْ وَذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالنُّورِ﴾ the Quran ﴿الَّذِي أَنْزَلْنَا وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾. Mention:

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ﴾ the Day of Resurrection; ﴿ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغَابُنِ﴾: the believers outdo the disbelievers by taking the places and families they would have had in Paradise had they believed. ﴿وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صَالِحًا يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِ وَيُدْخِلْهُ﴾ — and in a reading with nūn in both verbs — ﴿جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا ذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ the Quran, ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ is it.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿مَا أَصَابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His decree; ﴿وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ﴾ in His saying that the affliction is by His decree, ﴿يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ﴾ to patience over it; ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ the clear.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ وَأَوْلَادِكُمْ عَدُوًّا لَكُمْ فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ﴾ lest you obey them in staying behind from good, such as jihad and emigration, for the occasion of revelation of the verse was obedience in that. ﴿وَإِنْ تَعْفُوا﴾ them for their holding you back from that good, pleading the hardship your separation causes them, ﴿وَتَصْفَحُوا وَتَغْفِرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ for you, distracting from the affairs of the Hereafter; ﴿وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾, so do not miss it by occupying yourselves with wealth and children.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾: abrogating His saying {اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ}; ﴿وَاسْمَعُوا﴾ what you are commanded, a hearing of acceptance, ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا﴾ Allah, ﴿وَأَنْفِقُوا﴾ in obedience ﴿خَيْرًا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an implied يَكُنْ, the apodosis of the command. ﴿وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ the winners.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾ by giving charity with a good heart, ﴿يُضَاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ﴾ — and in a reading [يُضَعِّفْهُ] with tashdīd — one for ten, up to seven hundred and more, ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾ what He wills; ﴿وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ﴾ rewarding obedience, ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ in punishing disobedience.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ﴾ the secret ﴿وَالشَّهَادَةِ﴾ the open, ﴿الْعَزِيزُ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His making.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) it, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted [word that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿الْمُلْكُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ﴾ conjoined to «له الملك»; ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both are attached to «قدير»; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it «[Translator's note: so in the source; the clause «خلقكم» is the ṣila of «الذي».]»; ﴿فَمِنْكُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and a fronted khabar; ﴿كافِرٌ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ; ﴿وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «منكم كافر»; ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ; ﴿بِما﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بصير»; ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «السموات»; ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَصَوَّرَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ﴾ conjoined to «صوركم». ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «السموات». ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ ما تُسِرُّونَ وَما تُعْلِنُونَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿بِذاتِ﴾ both are attached to «عليم»; ﴿الصُّدُورِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ﴾ the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke (al-istifhām al-inkārī al-tawbīkhī), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the kāf being its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ﴾ its fāʿil (agent), annexed to the relative noun; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَذاقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَبالَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿أَمْرِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُ﴾ «ذلك» is mubtadaʾ (subject), the bāʾ is a preposition, and «أنّ» and its noun; ﴿كانَتْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); ﴿تَأْتِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿رُسُلُهُمْ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and the clause «كانت..» is the khabar (predicate) of «أنّ», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أنّ» and what follows it is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the preposition, and both are attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; and the clause «تأتيهم» is the khabar of «كانت», and the clause «ذلك..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَقالُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَبَشَرٌ﴾ the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī); ﴿بَشَرٌ﴾ the fāʿil of an omitted verb that the mentioned one explains, and the interrogative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿يَهْدُونَنا﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position; ﴿فَكَفَرُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿وَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «كفروا». ﴿وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and two khabars, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»; ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa) [from «أنّ»], its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); ﴿لَنْ يُبْعَثُوا﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «لن», the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «زعم». ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer; ﴿وَرَبِّي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being «أقسم» (I swear). ﴿لَتُبْعَثُنَّ﴾ the lām falls in the answer to the oath, and a passive imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the nūn having been dropped because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, is the nāʾib fāʿil, and the clause is the answer to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «لتبعثن». ﴿بِما﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿عَمِلْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila of «ما». ﴿وَذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to «يسير»; ﴿يَسِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فَآمِنُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is the apodosis of the implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty; ﴿وَالنُّورِ﴾ also conjoined; ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «النور»; ﴿أَنْزَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿بِما﴾ both are attached to «خبير»; ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the ṣila; ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ﴾ an adverb of time, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿لِيَوْمِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْجَمْعِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿ذلِكَ يَوْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿التَّغابُنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun making the verb jussive, mubtadaʾ; ﴿يُؤْمِنْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil being latent; ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿وَيَعْمَلْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يؤمن»; ﴿صالِحاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿يُكَفِّرْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «من», and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿سَيِّئاتِهِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَيُدْخِلْهُ﴾ conjoined to «يكفر», the hāʾ being its first object; ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ its second object; ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات» «[Translator's note: so in the source, although the fāʿil of «تجري» is «الأنهار», as the source itself says below.]». ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فِيها﴾ both are attached to «خالدين»; ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ a naʿt, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the relative noun is mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»; ﴿وَكَذَّبُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «كفروا»; ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the khabar of «الذين», and the clause «الذين..» is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿النَّارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فِيها﴾ both are attached to «خالدين»; ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿ما﴾ negating; ﴿أَصابَ﴾ a past verb, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; ﴿مُصِيبَةٍ﴾ genitive (majrūr) in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, the fāʿil (agent) of «أصاب»; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أصاب», the Name of Majesty being muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مِنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject) «[Translator's note: the source prints «مِنْ»; the word in the verse is «مَنْ».]»; ﴿يُؤْمِنْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿يَهْدِ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); ﴿قَلْبَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «من». And the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ; ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ both are attached to «عليم»; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ khabar, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), the Name of Majesty being its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أطيعوا الله». ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a conditional particle making the verb jussive; ﴿تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of reason (taʿlīl); ﴿إنما﴾ the restraining [«ما»] and the restrained [«إنّ»] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿عَلى رَسُولِنَا﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿الْبَلاغُ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation; ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun, its khabar (predicate) being omitted; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿هُوَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar, and the clause «لا إله..» is the khabar of the Name of Majesty. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is redundant (zāʾida); ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what comes after them; ﴿فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; ﴿الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; ﴿مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ﴾ the fronted khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; ﴿وَأَوْلادِكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أزواجكم»; ﴿عَدُوًّا﴾ the delayed noun of «إنّ»; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عدوا», and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِنْ تَعْفُوا﴾ «إن» is a conditional particle making the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the wāw being its fāʿil; ﴿وَتَصْفَحُوا وَتَغْفِرُوا﴾ both are conjoined to «تعفوا»; ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis, and «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ its two khabars, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis.

daas-irab:15-15.t: «[Translator's note: the source text of this entry is garbled — the opening letters of the Quranic words and their brackets have been lost and run into the analysis. It is translated here as it can be read; the Quranic words are restored in «…» from the verse.]» «إِنَّما» the restraining [«ما»] and the restrained [«إنّ»] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); «أَمْوالُكُمْ» mubtadaʾ (subject); «وَأَوْلادُكُمْ» conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أموالكم»; «فِتْنَةٌ» the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ» the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ, and an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; «أَجْرٌ» a delayed mubtadaʾ; «عَظِيمٌ» a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause «الله..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), the Name of Majesty being its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the apodosis of the implied condition, with no grammatical position; ﴿مَا﴾ maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); ﴿اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «ما» and the verb is in the accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. «استطاعتكم وجهدكم» (your capacity and your effort); ﴿وَاسْمَعُوا وَأَطِيعُوا وَأَنْفِقُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; ﴿خَيْراً﴾ the object of an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. «وائتوا خيرا» (and do good); ﴿لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خيرا»; ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يُوقَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿شُحَّ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿نَفْسِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ; ﴿هُمُ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the two clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «من».

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿إِنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ﴾ «إن» is a conditional particle making the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent) and the Name of Majesty the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿قَرْضاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿حَسَناً﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُضاعِفْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the hāʾ being its mafʿūl bihi and the fāʿil latent (mustatir); ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position; ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «يضاعفه»; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to «يغفر». ﴿وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and two khabars (predicates), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿عالِمُ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَالشَّهادَةِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الغيب»; ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ two khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ.

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) يسبّح is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); لله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسبّح, or the lām is redundant (zāʾida) with the object, and this has been discussed before. ما is the fāʿil (agent), and في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; وما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات.
(لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) له is a fronted khabar (predicate) and الملك a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); وله الحمد is conjoined to له الملك. هو is a mubtadaʾ, على كل شيء is attached to قدير, and قدير is the khabar of هو.
(هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ فَمِنْكُمْ كافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ) هو is a mubtadaʾ and الذي its khabar, and the clause خلقكم is the ṣila. The fāʾ is a conjunction; منكم is a fronted khabar and كافر a postponed mubtadaʾ; ومنكم مؤمن is conjoined to فمنكم كافر.
(وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ, بما is attached to بصير, the clause تعملون is the ṣila, and بصير is the khabar of الله.
(خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ) خلق is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring back to Allah; السموات is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and الأرض is conjoined to السموات. بالحق is a ḥāl, i.e. "joined with the truth", so the bāʾ is for accompaniment (al-mulābasa).
(وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ) The wāw is a conjunction; صوّركم is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. فأحسن is conjoined to وصوّركم, and صوركم is the mafʿūl bihi. إليه is a fronted khabar and المصير a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَيَعْلَمُ ما تُسِرُّونَ وَما تُعْلِنُونَ) يعلم is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "He", referring back to Allah the Exalted; ما is the mafʿūl bihi, and في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; وما في الأرض is conjoined; and ويعلم ما تسرّون وما تعلنون is also conjoined.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «له الملك وله الحمد» there is fronting (taqdīm): the khabar is fronted in both to indicate that the two matters are exclusive to Him, the Exalted.
2- In the preceding verses there is antithesis (ṭibāq) between السموات and الأرض, between كافر and مؤمن, and between تسرّون and تعلنون.
3- Al-Zamakhsharī has a question and answer that are exceedingly delightful, which we quote below: «If you ask: how did He make their forms beautiful? I answer: He made them the most beautiful and splendid of all animals, the proof being that a human being does not wish that his form were other than it is, whatever other forms he sees. Part of the beauty of his form is that he was created upright, not stooping, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "in the best of stature". If you ask: how many an ugly person is there, of disfigured form and repulsive build, whom eyes despise? I answer: there is no repulsiveness there; rather beauty, like other qualities, comes in levels and ranks. Because some forms fall clearly below the ranks of those above them, and when compared with what surpasses them, they are not found pleasing; otherwise they are within the domain of beauty and do not go outside its bounds. Do you not see that you may admire a form and find it pleasing, then see one more pleasing and higher in the ranks of beauty than it, so that your eye shrinks from the first and you find it burdensome to look at it, after having been infatuated with it and having doted on it? The sages said: two things have no limit: beauty and eloquence».

dervis-irab:5-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ) الوبال originally means heaviness; from it comes الوبيل for food that lies heavy on the stomach, and الوابل for heavy rain; then it was borrowed for punishment, because it is like a heavy, tangible thing. In the lexicons: الوبال is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of وبل. One says وَبُلَ, of the pattern ẓarufa, yawbulu, wablan, wabālan, wubūlan and wabālatan: [of] a place, it was unwholesome; [of] a thing, it became severe. And وَبَلَ, of the pattern ḍaraba, yabilu, wablan: [وبل] فلانا بالعصا, he beat him with the stick with successive blows; [وبل] الصيد, he chased the game hard. وبلت السماء: the sky poured down heavy rain (al-wabl). استوبل istībālan [of] a place: he found it unwholesome; استوبلت الإبل: the camels feigned sickness from the unwholesomeness of their pasture.
(زَعَمَ) al-zaʿm is claiming knowledge, and it takes two objects. From it is his saying, upon him be blessing and peace: «"They claimed" (زعموا) is the mount of lying». From Shurayḥ: everything has a kunya, and the kunya of lying is "they claimed". Most often زعم falls upon أنْ with the nūn lightened or أنّ with it doubled, with fatḥa on the hamza in both.
(التَّغابُنِ) tafāʿul from al-ghabn, and it is not between two parties but from one, like تواضع and تحامل. Al-ghabn is taking something for less than its value, or selling it likewise. It has also been said that al-ghabn is concealment; from it comes ghabn in selling, because it is concealed. One says غبن الثوب and خبنته when you take up what of it is longer than your measure; so its meaning is diminution. More discussion of التغابن will come in the section on rhetoric.
Moreover, the ghayn together with the bāʾ, as the first and second radicals of a word, has a particular signification of concealment, absence and hiding. One says لحم غاب, i.e. meat kept overnight, and there is the sense of concealment in it. The thicket (al-ghāba) is so called because it conceals whoever is within it, being crowded with trees. زرته غبًّا: I visited him now and then, and the sense of absence from his companion in it is not hidden. Ḥumayd ibn Thawb [Translator's note: so in the source; the poet is usually named Ḥumayd ibn Thawr] said:
زور مغب ومأمول أخو ثقة ... وسائر من ثناء الصدق مشهور
(A visitor who comes at intervals, a trustworthy brother in whom one places hope, and one widely known for truthful praise.)
And you say: love increases with visiting at intervals (al-ighbāb) and decreases with constant attendance (al-ikbāb). ماء غِبّ and مياه أغباب, i.e. distant water that is reached only after an interval. المغبّة is the outcome of a thing, and it is hidden, known only by conjecture. الغابر is the past, and there is no doubt about its being absent; it also comes with the meaning of "remaining", so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). اغبرّ, with doubled rāʾ, means it became dusty, and [of] the day, its dust grew intense. Those who recite poetry with melodies, are moved to ecstasy, dance and make a commotion are called al-mughabbira, and their ecstatic singing is called al-taghbīr; it is their habit to keep out of sight and hidden. From al-Shāfiʿī: I think the heretics (al-zanādiqa) devised this taghbīr to turn people away from the remembrance of Allah and from reciting the Quran. جاء على ظهر الغبراء والغبيراء, i.e. on the back of the earth, meaning on foot. «The green [sky] has not shaded, nor has the dusty [earth] borne, anyone more truthful in speech than Abū Dharr». The needy are called بنو الغبراء; Ṭarafa said:
رأيت بني الغبراء لا ينكرونني ... ولا أهل هذاك الطراف الممدّد
(I saw that the sons of the dust do not disown me, nor do the people of that outstretched leather tent.)
وزففن إليّ ذئبة غبساء [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently "they led a dusky she-wolf to me in procession", an idiom cited without explanation]. And you say: لن يبلغ دبيس ما غبا غبيس, "Dubays will not attain [it] as long as Ghubays is hidden"; it [غبيس] is a proper name for the constellation al-Jady, so called because of its being hidden. خرج في الغبش, he went out in the dusk of the end of night, and نحن في أغباش الليل, we are in the remnants of the night. فلان يتغبّش الناس, i.e. he wrongs them, and it is obvious that he will not confront them openly with wrongdoing [Translator's note: the source's «وبديه أنه لن يبادهم» is unclear; rendered as best as can be read]. غبط الكبش: he felt the ram's back to know its fatness; and غبطه, of the patterns ḍaraba and ʿalima: he was great in his eyes and he wished for the like of his condition without wanting it to cease from him. الغبيط is the saddle on which the howdah is fastened, so it hides the woman riding in it; Imruʾ al-Qays said:
تقول وقد مال الغبيط بنا معا ... عقرت بعيري يا امرأ القيس فانزل
(She says, while the saddle leaned with both of us together: "You have galled my camel, O Imruʾ al-Qays, so get down.")
غبقه, of the patterns naṣara and ḍaraba: he gave him al-ghabūq to drink, which is wine drunk in the evening, when the night hides them [Translator's note: the source prints «يخيفهم» "frightens them", evidently for «يخفيهم» "hides them"]. غبي يغبى غبًا and غباوة the thing, or [غبي] عنه: he did not perceive it or was ignorant of it; and [غبي] الشيء عليه: it was hidden from him and he did not know it. One says: there is in so-and-so a dullness (غباوة) that provides for him; and most of the rich are dull (أغبياء); and what you did is not hidden from me (لا يغبى عليّ). الغباء is hidden ground. This is one of the wonders of our language, so ponder it.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ فَذاقُوا وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) The hamza is for a disapproving, rebuking interrogative, or an affirming, rebuking one. لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; يأتكم is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and نبأ the fāʿil (agent); الذين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause كفروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من قبل is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The fāʾ is a conjunction; ذاقوا is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, the wāw is the fāʿil, and وبال أمرهم is the mafʿūl bihi. The wāw is a conjunction; لهم is a fronted khabar (predicate), عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and أليم a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُ كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ) ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the two punishments of this world and the Hereafter; بأنه is the khabar. أنّ and its noun, and the clause كانت is its khabar; the noun of كانت is latent (mustatir), referring to the messengers, and the clause تأتيهم is the khabar; رسلهم is the fāʿil of تأتيهم, and بالبيّنات is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تأتيهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the more usual parsing makes the hāʾ of أنه the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and رسلهم the noun of كانت].
(فَقالُوا أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قالوا is a past verb and its fāʿil, conjoined to كانت. The hamza is for a disapproving interrogative; بشر is a mubtadaʾ, its being a subject made permissible by the interrogative entering upon it. They have also permitted it to be nominative as the fāʿil of an implied verb explained by what follows, so the question belongs to the chapter of al-ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), the implied form being "Will a human being guide us?" The clause يهدوننا is in the position of nominative as a khabar on the first view, and has no grammatical position on the second, because it is explicative. The interrogative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(فَكَفَرُوا وَتَوَلَّوْا وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ) The fāʾ is a conjunction and conveys causation, not immediate succession, i.e. "so they disbelieved because of this saying". وتولّوا is conjoined to فكفروا; استغنى الله is a verb and its fāʿil. الله is a mubtadaʾ, غني a first khabar and حميد a second khabar.
(زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ لَنْ يُبْعَثُوا قُلْ بَلى وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ) زعم is a past verb and الذين its fāʿil; the clause كفروا is the ṣila. أنْ is lightened from the heavy [anna], its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity, and the clause is the khabar of أن; أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of زعم. قل is an imperative verb; بلى is a particle of answer affirming [what was] negated. The wāw is the wāw of oath and ربي is genitive by the wāw of oath, the two being attached to the omitted verb of swearing. The lām occurs in the response to the oath; تبعثنّ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, is the wāw of the plural, an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil [Translator's note: the source says «وعلامة رفعه حذف النون» "the sign of its nominative is the dropping of the nūn"; what is meant is the nūn, which has been dropped; and since the verb is passive, the wāw is strictly the nāʾib fāʿil].
(ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِما عَمِلْتُمْ وَذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ) ثم is a conjunction for sequence with an interval; لتنبؤنّ is conjoined to لتبعثنّ; بما is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause عملتم is the ṣila. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to what was mentioned of resurrection and reckoning; على الله is attached to يسير, and يسير is the khabar of ذلك.
(فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالنُّورِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْنا) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), because it occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the matter is so, then believe". آمنوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and بالله is attached to آمنوا; رسوله is conjoined to الله, and النور is also conjoined; الذي is a naʿt, and the clause أنزلنا is an adjective [i.e. the ṣila], the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. أنزلناه.
(وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); الله is a mubtadaʾ, بما is attached to خبير, the clause تعملون is the ṣila, and خبير is the khabar of الله.
(يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ ذلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ) يوم is an adverb attached to خبير, or to something omitted indicated by the context of the speech, i.e. "you will differ on the day He gathers you". It has also been said that it is the object of an omitted verb, i.e. "remember". The clause يجمعكم is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and ليوم الجمع is attached to يجمعكم; it is so named because on it Allah gathers together the first and the last to carry out the reckoning and the recompense. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the Day of Gathering, and يوم التغابن is its khabar, i.e. the believers will get the better of the disbelievers by taking their places. More about its meaning will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صالِحاً يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ) The wāw is resumptive and the clause is new, set out to explain the mutual loss and gain (al-taghābun) and give its details. من is a jussivizing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يؤمن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and بالله is attached to يؤمن; يعمل is conjoined to يؤمن, and صالحا is a mafʿūl bihi or a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a righteous deed". يكفّر is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), عنه is attached to يكفّر, and سيئاته is the mafʿūl bihi. The protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of من.
(وَيُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ) ويدخله is conjoined to يكفّر, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is a naʿt of جنات. خالدين is a ḥāl, and it is plural because it refers back to the meaning of من, which is plural; فيها is attached to خالدين, and أبدا is an adverb attached to خالدين. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to what was mentioned of expiation and admission to the gardens; الفوز is the khabar and العظيم a naʿt of الفوز.
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ خالِدِينَ فِيها وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) The wāw is a conjunction; الذين is a mubtadaʾ and the clause كفروا is the ṣila; كذبوا is conjoined to كفروا, and بآياتنا is attached to كذبوا. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب النار the khabar; خالدين is a ḥāl and فيها is attached to خالدين. بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame, المصير is the fāʿil, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "it", i.e. the Fire.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «ذلك يوم التغابن» there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya). The state of the two parties who were able to choose what leads to happiness in the Hereafter, each party choosing what it desired of what it was capable of in place of what the other chose, was likened to the state of those exchanging goods in trade; and what branches out from that, namely each of them taking the other's place, was likened to al-taghābun, because taghābun is tafāʿul from al-ghabn, which is taking a thing from its owner for less than its value; and that only occurs in a contract of exchange, and there is no exchange in the Hereafter. So applying taghābun to what happens there is only by way of representational metaphor. Al-Zamakhsharī's words are: «al-taghābun is borrowed from people's taghābun in trade, which is that some of them get the better of others, because of the blessed taking the places of the wretched which they [the wretched] would have taken had they been blessed, and the wretched taking the places of the blessed which they [the blessed] would have taken had they been wretched».
2- In the verse there is also the figure of mockery (al-tahakkum), which has been met with before. Here He mocks the wretched, because their taking [those places] is not a gain. In the ḥadīth: «There is no servant who enters the Garden except that he is shown his seat in the Fire had he done evil, so that he may increase in gratitude; and there is no servant who enters the Fire except that he is shown his seat in the Garden had he done good, so that he may increase in regret». And in another ḥadīth: «People go out in the morning in two ways: one who buys his soul and thus frees it, and one who buys his soul and thus destroys it».

dervis-irab:11-18.t:
* I'rab:
(ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) A new (mustaʾnaf) statement set out to reply to the disbelievers who said: if the Muslims were in the right, Allah would protect them from calamities in this world. ما is negating and أصاب a past verb; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and مصيبة is genitive (majrūr) in wording and nominative (marfūʿ) in position as the fāʿil (agent); the object of أصاب is omitted, i.e. "anyone". إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and بإذن الله is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أصاب.
(وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussivizing conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); يؤمن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and بالله is attached to يؤمن. يهد is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and قلبه is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من. الله is a mubtadaʾ, بكل شيء is attached to عليم, and عليم is the khabar of الله.
(وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَإِنَّما عَلى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ) The wāw is a conjunction; أطيعوا is an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil and الله the mafʿūl bihi; وأطيعوا الرسول is conjoined to أطيعوا الله. The fāʾ is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); إن is a jussivizing conditional particle and توليتم is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then there is no harm to Our Messenger in your turning away". The fāʾ is a particle of causation; إنما is [إنّ] made inoperative by [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); على رسولنا is fronted [Translator's note: i.e. a fronted khabar], البلاغ a postponed mubtadaʾ, and المبين a naʿt (adjective) of البلاغ.
(اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ) الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا إله إلا هو is the khabar; the i'rab of the word of testimony has been given in detail earlier. على الله is attached to يتوكل; the fāʾ is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of command, يتوكل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām, and المؤمنون is the fāʿil.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ مِنْ أَزْواجِكُمْ وَأَوْلادِكُمْ عَدُوًّا لَكُمْ فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ) The i'rab of يا أيها الذين آمنوا has been given many times. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; من أزواجكم is the fronted khabar of إنّ and أولادكم is conjoined to أزواجكم; عدوا is the postponed noun of إنّ and لكم a naʿt of عدوا. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you know that, then beware of them". احذروهم is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi.
(وَإِنْ تَعْفُوا وَتَصْفَحُوا وَتَغْفِرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is a jussivizing conditional particle and تعفوا is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; تصفحوا is conjoined to تعفوا, and تغفروا is also conjoined. The fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a nominal clause; إنّ, its noun and its two khabars.
(إِنَّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ) [Translator's note: in the source the heading of this verse and of the next segment are run together with the preceding text by a typesetting fault; they are restored here.] إنما is [إنّ] made inoperative by [ما]; أموالكم is a mubtadaʾ, أولادكم is conjoined to أموالكم, and فتنة is the khabar.
(وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ) The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; عنده is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar, أجر is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and عظيم a naʿt of أجر; the clause is the khabar of الله.
(فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ وَاسْمَعُوا وَأَطِيعُوا وَأَنْفِقُوا خَيْراً لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. "if you know that He, the Exalted, has made your wealth and your children a trial for you, distracting you from the affairs of the Hereafter, then fear Allah". ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "[with] your effort and your ability". اسمعوا, أطيعوا and أنفقوا are imperative verbs conjoined to اتقوا. As for خيرا, there are [several views] about it:
1- The view of Sībawayh, that it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and bring good for yourselves", like His saying: «انتهوا خيرا لكم»; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ confined themselves to this.
2- The view of Abū ʿUbayda, that it is the khabar of an implied يكن, i.e. "the agreement (al-ittifāq) will be good" [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «الإنفاق» "the spending"].
3- The view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, that it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a good spending".
4- The view of the Kufans, that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
5- The view of some, that it is the mafʿūl bihi of His saying أنفقوا, on the assumption of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "good wealth".
لأنفسكم is attached to خبيرا [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently for «بخيرا», i.e. attached to خيرا].
(وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; من is a jussivizing conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يوق is the protasis, jussive by the dropping of the weak letter, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Translator's note: the source prints «نائب الفعل», evidently for «نائب الفاعل»] is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he"; شحّ نفسه is a second mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ links the apodosis, and the clause فأولئك هم المفلحون is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.
(إِنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً يُضاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ) إن is conditional and تقرضوا is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and الله its object; قرضا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and حسنا a naʿt. يضاعفه is the apodosis, the hāʾ is its object, and لكم is attached to يضاعفه.
(وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ) ويغفر is conjoined to the apodosis, following it in the jussive, and لكم is attached to يغفر. الله is a mubtadaʾ, شكور a first khabar and حليم a second khabar.
(عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) عالم الغيب is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, العزيز a second khabar and الحكيم a third khabar.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَآ أَصَابَ مِن مُّصِيبَةٍ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He means: except by Allah's command. ﴿وَمَن يُؤْمِن بِٱللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ﴾ at the time of calamity, so that he says: "We belong to Allah and to Him we return". It is also said: He guides his heart, so that when he is tried he is patient, when he is blessed he is grateful, and when he is wronged he forgives; that is His saying: يهد قلبه [200/a].

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِنَّ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ وَأَوْلاَدِكُمْ عَدُوّاً لَّكُمْ فَٱحْذَرُوهُمْ﴾.
It came down when people were commanded to emigrate from Mecca to Medina. When a man wanted to emigrate, his wife and children would cling to him and say: Where will you put us, and to whom will you leave us? So he would take pity on them and stay behind, failing to emigrate. That is His saying: ﴿فَٱحْذَرُوهُمْ﴾, i.e. do not obey them in staying behind.
His saying: ﴿وَإِن تَعْفُواْ وَتَصْفَحُواْ﴾.
It came down concerning the children of those who emigrated and did not obey their families; for they had said to them when parting from them for the emigration: If you do not follow us, we will not spend on you. Then they joined them afterwards in Medina, and they did not spend on them, until they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and there came down: "If you pardon and overlook" — and spend on them. So He gave them a dispensation to spend on them.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ﴾.
It is said: whoever pays the zakat has been protected from the avarice of his soul. Some of the readers read "ومَنْ يُوقَ شِحَّ نَفْسِه" with kasra on the shīn, but reading it with ḍamma [شُحّ] is predominant in recitation.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The clause «له الملك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the Divine Name, and the clause «وهو على كل شيء قدير» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «له الملك».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «هو الذي» is resumptive; the clause «فمنكم كافر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «هو الذي»; the clause «والله بصير» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بصير».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «خلق» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خلق»; the clause «وصوَّركم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «خلق»; the clause «فأحسن» is conjoined to the clause «صوَّركم»; and the clause «وإليه المصير» is conjoined to the clause «خلق».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «والله عليم» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «بذات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عليم».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The preposition phrase «من قبل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يأتكم»; the clause «فذاقوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كفروا»; the clause «ولهم عذاب» is conjoined to the clause «ذاقوا».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: (ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the noun of «كانت» is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), and the clause «تأتيهم رسلهم» is the khabar of «كانت»; it is weak to take «رسلهم» as the noun of kāna and the clause «تأتيهم» as the khabar, because the khabar of a mubtadaʾ (subject), when it is a verbal clause, does not precede the mubtadaʾ. The preposition phrase «بالبينات» is attached to «تأتيهم»; the clause «فقالوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «كانت»; the clause «يهدوننا» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, even though it is most common for the hamza to be followed by a verb; the clause «فكفروا» is conjoined to the clause «قالوا»; the clause «واستغنى الله» is conjoined to the clause «تولَّوا»; the pronoun in «يهدوننا» is plural because «البشر» is a generic noun (ism jins).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «أن» is lightened from the heavy [أنَّ], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لن يبعثوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أن» and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «زعم»; the clause «بلى وربي لتبعثن» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause «لتبعثن» is the answer to the oath; and the clause «وذلك على الله يسير» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «فآمنوا» is resumptive; «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause «والله خبير» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «يوم» is the object of the implied verb «اذكر» (remember); the clause «ذلك يوم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «يوم الجمع»; the conditional clause is resumptive; «جنات» is a second object; «أبدا» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خالدين»; the clause «ذلك الفوز» is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «والذين كفروا..» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ} and has no grammatical position; the clause «أولئك أصحاب» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; the clause «وبئس المصير» is resumptive, and the one specified [for blame] (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted, i.e.: the Fire.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: His words «مصيبة»: the fāʿil (agent) of «أصاب», and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the object is omitted, its implied form being "أحدًا" (anyone); the preposition phrase «بإذن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مصيبة»; the conditional clause is resumptive, and likewise the clause «والله بكل شيء عليم».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «وأطيعوا» is resumptive; the conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause; the preposition phrase «على رسولنا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «البلاغ».

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: (الله لا إله إلا هو) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause of transcendence is the khabar (predicate); the clause «وعلى الله فليتوكل» is resumptive; the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يتوكل».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «إن من أزواجكم», the answer to the vocative, is resumptive; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عدوا»; the clause «فاحذروهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause of the answer to the vocative; the conditional clause is conjoined to the answer to the vocative; «رحيم» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «إنما» is a restraining [particle] and restrained [particle] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); the clause «والله عنده أجر» is resumptive; the clause «عنده أجر» is the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «فاتقوا» is resumptive; «ما» is maṣdariyya and temporal (maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ما استطعتم» is accusative as an adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اتقوا», the implied form being: for the duration of your ability; «خيرا»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: a good spending, its adjective standing in for it. «شح» is a second object; «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «قرضا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause «والله شكور» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: His words «عالم»: a third khabar (predicate) of the Divine Name, and «العزيز الحكيم» are further khabars.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying, Exalted is He, أبشر يهدوننا: يهدوننا was put in the plural only because He referred it back to the meaning of بشر, since it has the meaning of a group in this place; and it may be used for the singular, as in His saying ما هذا بشرا. [Translator's note: the edition prints «تَنْفِي» here, which appears to be a corruption of «في» ("in").] The grammarians permitted رأيت ثلاثة نفر and ثلاثة رهط ("I saw three persons"), construing according to the meaning, but they did not permit رأيت ثلاثة قوم nor ثلاثة بشر. The difference between them is that نفر and رهط are for numbers below ten, so a number below ten was annexed to them, since it is its counterpart; whereas قوم may apply to numbers above ten, so it was not good to annex a number below ten to what is above it. As for بشر, it applies to a single person, so it was not possible to annex a number to a singular. بشر is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is also said: by an implied verb.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying يَوْم يجمعكم: يوم is an adverb, and the governing word in it is ثم لتنبؤن.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying وأنفقوا خيرا: خير is accusative according to Sībawayh by an implied verb indicated by the speech, because when He said وأنفقوا it indicated that He commanded them to do an act of good; so it is as if He said "and do good" (وأتوا خيرا). Abū ʿUbayda said it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied كان, i.e. "it will be good" (يكن خيرا). Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī said it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "and spend a good spending" (وأنفقوا إنفاقا خيرا). It is also said that it is accusative by أنفقوا, الخير being wealth on this view, and there is remoteness in it in meaning. Some of the Kufans said it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and that too is remote in meaning and in i'rab.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿إن تقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا يضاعفه لكم﴾: «إن» is conditional; «تقرضوا» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its being jussive (majzūm) being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Name of Majesty is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «قرضًا» stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); «حسنًا» is a naʿt (adjective); «يضاعفه» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is its object; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يضاعفه﴾.
﴿ويغفر لكم والله شكور حليم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «يغفر» is conjoined to the apodosis and follows it in the jussive; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يغفر﴾; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «شكور» is a first khabar (predicate), and «حليم» is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿عالم الغيب والشهادة العزيز الحكيم﴾: «عالم الغيب» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); «العزيز» is a second khabar, and «الحكيم» is a third khabar.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يسبح﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿لله﴾: the lām is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسبح﴾, or the lām is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) on the object.
﴿ما﴾: the fāʿil (agent).
﴿في السماوات﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾; and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿وما في الأرض﴾: conjoined to ما في السماوات.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿الملك﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وله الحمد﴾: conjoined to له الملك.
﴿وهو﴾: the mubtadaʾ.
﴿على كل شيء﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدير﴾.
﴿قدير﴾: the khabar of هو.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن﴾: هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and الذي is its khabar (predicate); the clause خلقكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The fāʾ is a conjunction; منكم is a fronted khabar and كافر a postponed mubtadaʾ; and منكم مؤمن is conjoined to فمنكم كافر.
﴿والله بما تعملون بصير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; الله is the mubtadaʾ; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بصير﴾; the clause تعملون is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and بصير is the khabar of the Word of Majesty الله.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق﴾: خلق is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring back to Allah; السماوات is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الأرض is conjoined to السماوات; and بالحق is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "accompanied by the truth", so the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa).
﴿وصوركم فأحسن صوركم وإليه المصير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; صوركم is a past verb, a latent fāʿil, and a mafʿūl bihi; فأحسن is conjoined to وصوركم; صوركم is the mafʿūl bihi; إليه is a fronted khabar (predicate); and المصير is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿يعلم ما في السماوات والأرض ويعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون﴾: يعلم is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو), referring back to Allah the Exalted; ما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في السماوات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ما في الأرض is conjoined; and يعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون is also conjoined.
﴿والله عليم بذات الصدور﴾: conjoined to the first يعلم.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين كفروا من قبل فذاقوا وبال أمرهم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke, or of affirmation and rebuke; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; يأتكم is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); نبأ is the fāʿil (agent); الذين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause كفروا has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كفروا﴾; the fāʾ is a conjunction; ذاقوا is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and وبال أمرهم is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ولهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لهم is a fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿عذاب﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أليم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذاب﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ذلك بأنه كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات﴾: ذلك is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the two punishments of this world and the Hereafter; بأنه is the khabar (predicate); أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun (ism); the clause كانت is its khabar; the noun of كانت is latent (mustatir), referring back to the messengers; the clause تأتيهم is the khabar; رسلهم is the fāʿil (agent) of تأتيهم; and بالبينات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تأتيهم.
﴿فقالوا أبشر يهدوننا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction. قالوا is a past verb and its fāʿil, and it is conjoined to كانت. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval. بشر is nominative (marfūʿ) as fāʿil of an implied verb indicated by what follows it, so the matter belongs to the chapter of "preoccupation" (al-ishtighāl), the implied form being ﴿أيهدينا بشر﴾; and the clause ﴿يهدوننا﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position. It has also been said that ﴿بشر﴾ is an indefinite mubtadaʾ, which may begin the sentence because the interrogative enters upon it, and the clause ﴿يهدوننا﴾ is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The interrogative clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿فكفروا وتولوا واستغنى الله والله غني حميد﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and it expresses causation, not immediate sequence, i.e. "so they disbelieved because of this saying"; تولوا is conjoined to فكفروا; استغنى الله is a verb and its fāʿil; الله is a mubtadaʾ; غني is the first khabar and حميد the second khabar.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿زعم الذين كفروا أن لن يبعثوا قل بلى وربي لتبعثن﴾: زعم is a past verb, and الذين is its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], and its noun (ism) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted; لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; the clause ﴿لن يبعثوا...﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the lightened أن; and أن together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of زعم. قل is an imperative verb; بلى is a particle of reply, for cancelling the negation and affirming the resurrection; the wāw is the wāw of the oath; ربي: the word is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath, and the two are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of swearing; the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; تبعثن is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the nūn, dropped because of the succession of like letters; and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the wāw of the group, an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative as fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source; تُبعثُنّ is passive, so on the usual analysis this wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)].
﴿ثم لتنبؤن بما عملتم وذلك﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; لتنبؤن is conjoined to لتبعثن; بما is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause عملتم is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to what has been mentioned of the resurrection and the reckoning.
﴿على الله﴾: على is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يسير﴾.
﴿يسير﴾: the khabar of ذلك.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فآمنوا بالله ورسوله والنور الذي أنزلنا﴾: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), because it occurs in the apodosis of a supplied condition, i.e. "if the matter is so, then believe"; آمنوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); in بالله the bāʾ is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنوا; رسوله is conjoined to الله; النور is also conjoined; الذي is a naʿt (adjective); the clause أنزلنا is an adjective (ṣifa) [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause is the ṣila of الذي]; and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "We sent it down" (أنزلناه).
﴿والله بما تعملون خبير﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خبير﴾; the clause تعملون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; خبير is the khabar (predicate) of the Word of Majesty; and the clause ﴿والله بما...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع ذلك يوم التغابن﴾: يوم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) خبير, or to something omitted indicated by the context of the speech, i.e. "you will differ on the day He gathers you"; it has also been said that it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "remember the day He gathers you"; the clause يجمعكم is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ليوم الجمع is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يجمعكم; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to the Day of Gathering; and يوم التغابن is its khabar (predicate).
﴿ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا يكفر عنه سيئاته﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; يؤمن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); in بالله the bāʾ is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يؤمن﴾; يعمل is conjoined to يؤمن; صالحًا is the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يعمل﴾, or a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of the maṣdar, i.e. "does a righteous deed". يكفر is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عنه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكفر﴾; سيئاته is the mafʿūl bihi; and the protasis together with the requital is the khabar of من.
﴿ويدخله جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يدخله is conjoined to يكفر; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is a naʿt (adjective) of جنات; خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is plural because it refers back to the meaning of من, which is plural; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدين; أبدًا is an adverb attached to خالدين; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to what has been mentioned of the expiation and the admission into the gardens; الفوز is the khabar; and العظيم is a naʿt of الفوز.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; الذين is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; كذبوا is conjoined to كفروا; and بآياتنا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبوا﴾.
﴿أولئك أصحاب النار خالدين فيها وبئس المصير﴾: أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب النار the khabar (predicate); خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدين; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; المصير is the fāʿil (agent); and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "it" (هي), i.e. the Fire.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿ما أصاب من مصيبة إلا بإذن الله﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ما is negative; أصاب is a past verb; من is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and مصيبة is genitive in form and nominative in position, as the fāʿil (agent); the object of أصاب is omitted, i.e. "anyone"; إلا is a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); and بإذن الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أصاب﴾.
﴿ومن يؤمن بالله يهد قلبه والله بكل شيء عليم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); يؤمن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); in بالله the bāʾ is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يؤمن﴾; يهد is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; قلبه is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the protasis together with the requital is the khabar (predicate) of من; الله is a mubtadaʾ; بكل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عليم﴾; and عليم is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وأطيعوا الله وأطيعوا الرسول﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أطيعوا is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and أطيعوا الرسول is conjoined to أطيعوا الله.
﴿فإن توليتم فإنما على رسولنا البلاغ المبين﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; إن is a jussive-governing conditional particle; توليتم is a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then there is no harm to Our Messenger in your turning away"; the fāʾ is a particle of cause (taʿlīl); إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); على رسولنا is fronted [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "a fronted khabar (predicate)" is meant]; البلاغ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and المبين is a naʿt (adjective) of البلاغ.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿الله﴾: the mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
﴿إله﴾: its noun (ism), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr).
﴿هو﴾: a badal (substitute) from the position of لا together with its noun, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (al-ibtidāʾ); or a badal from the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar (predicate). The clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is the khabar of ﴿الله﴾.
﴿وعلى الله﴾: على is a preposition and the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتوكل﴾.
﴿فليتوكل المؤمنون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; يتوكل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām; and المؤمنون is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position. ﴿يا أيها﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); and ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh). الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾. ﴿آمنوا﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿إن من أزواجكم وأولادكم عدوا لكم فاحذروهم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); من أزواجكم is the fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; أولادكم is conjoined to أزواجكم; عدوًّا is the postponed noun (ism) of إن; لكم is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عدوًّا﴾; the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); and احذروهم is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وإن تعفوا وتصفحوا وتغفروا فإن الله غفور رحيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is a jussive-governing conditional particle; تعفوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; تصفحوا is conjoined to تعفوا, and تغفروا is also conjoined; the fāʾ links the apodosis, because it is a nominal clause; إن is an abrogating particle, the Word of Majesty (lafẓ al-jalāla) is its noun, غفور is its khabar, and رحيم is its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة﴾: إنما is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أموالكم is the mubtadaʾ (subject); أولادكم is conjoined to أموالكم; and فتنة is the khabar (predicate).
﴿والله عنده أجر عظيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; عنده is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; أجر is a postponed mubtadaʾ; عظيم is a naʿt (adjective) of أجر; the clause is the khabar of الله; and the clause ﴿والله عنده...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿فاتقوا الله ما استطعتم واسمعوا وأطيعوا وأنفقوا خيرا لأنفسكم﴾: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); اتقوا الله is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: so in the source; the fāʿil of اتقوا is in fact the overt wāw], and the object; ما is maṣdar-forming and, together with what follows it, is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, i.e. "[to the extent of] your effort and your ability". اسمعوا, أطيعوا and أنفقوا are imperative verbs conjoined to اتقوا; ﴿خيرًا﴾ is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and bring good for yourselves"; it has also been said that ﴿خيرا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of an implied يكن; it has also been said: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a spending that is good"; it has also been said: a ḥāl (circumstantial); and it has also been said: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). لأنفسكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خيرًا﴾.
﴿ومن يوق شح نفسه فأولئك هم المفلحون﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); يوق is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter; the "deputy of the verb" (nāʾib al-fiʿl) is latent, its implied form being "he" (هو) [Translator's note: so in the source; the deputy agent, nāʾib al-fāʿil, is meant]; شح is the second mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; the clause فأولئك هم المفلحون is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of من; and the clause ﴿ومن يوق شح نفسه...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ: this may be the end of the statement, or it may be connected, and لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ would then be "[that which is in the heavens] belongs to Him", or لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); that is, His authority, His command and His decree are carried out in both of them. وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: that is, possessed of power over whatever He wills: He creates what He wills, gives life and causes death, exalts and abases; nothing is beyond Him, because He is the possessor of perfect power.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ: if you wish, you may assimilate the qāf into the kāf. فَمِنْكُمْ كافِرٌ وَمِنْكُمْ مُؤْمِنٌ: that is, one who affirms, certain that He is his Creator and his God and that he has no god but Him. وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ: that is, knowing your deeds, so do not go against His command and His prohibition, lest He assail you.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ: that is, with justice and equity. وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ. From Abū Razīn: صَوَّرَكُمْ [read "ṣiwarakum"]: he likened the pattern fuʿla to fiʿla, just as fiʿla is likened to fuʿla. They said: kiswa and kusā, rishwa and rushā, and liḥya and luḥā is more frequent; and they said: quwwa and quwā. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is due to the affinity of the ḍamma with the kasra. وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ: that is, the return of all of you, and He will requite you for your deeds.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: the mīm may be assimilated into the mīm, and likewise وَيَعْلَمُ ما تُسِرُّونَ وَما تُعْلِنُونَ. The meaning is: and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose among yourselves of word and deed. وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ: that is, knowing what your breasts hide and what your souls enfold, which is more hidden than the secret.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ: the origin is "yaʾtīkum"; the yāʾ was dropped for the jussive (jazm). Whoever says "a-lam yaʾtīka", for him the origin is "yaʾtīka", and the ḍamma was dropped for the jussive; however, the first is the more eloquent usage. Sībawayh said: Know that when the final letter is quiescent in the nominative, it is dropped in the jussive. Abū Jaʿfar said:
I heard Abū Isḥāq say: we read before Muḥammad ibn Yazīd: "Know that when the final letter is quiescent in the nominative and the genitive, it is dropped in the jussive, so that the jussive should not be the same as the nominative and the genitive". فَذاقُوا وَبالَ أَمْرِهِمْ: that is, the punishment touched them for their disbelief. وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ: that is, in the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُ: the hāʾ is an allusion (kināya) to the matter (al-ḥadīth, i.e. the pronoun of the matter), and what follows it explains it and is the khabar (predicate) of "anna". كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ: that is, with the proofs and demonstrations. فَقالُوا أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنا: He said "yahdūnanā" (they guide us), while the word "bashar" is singular. The grammarians discussed the like of this. Some of them said: "yahdūnanā" is according to the meaning, and "yahdīnā" would be according to the wording. Al-Māzinī spoke — and he mentioned reasons in questions of grammar — among them that the grammarians permitted saying "jāʾanī thalāthatu nafarin" and "thalāthatu rahṭin" (three persons came to me), these two being collective nouns, yet did not permit "jāʾanī thalāthatu qawmin" or "thalāthatu basharin", although these two are, according to some grammarians, collective nouns. Al-Māzinī said: "jāʾanī thalāthatu nafarin" and "thalāthatu rahṭin" are permitted only because "nafar" and "rahṭ" are for the smallest numbers, so it fell in its proper place; whereas "bashar" is for a large number and "qawm" for small and large, so for that reason this was not permitted with them. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd disagreed with him in his reasoning about "bashar" and agreed with him in the rest, saying: "bashar" may be for the singular and the plural. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
ما هذا بَشَراً [Yūsuf: 31]. He said: for that reason "jāʾanī thalāthatu basharin" is not permitted. فَكَفَرُوا: that is, they denied the prophets of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His signs. وَتَوَلَّوْا: that is, they turned their backs on faith. وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ: from their faith. وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ: free of need of all His creation. حَمِيدٌ: that is, praised among them for the favours and bounty of His that they know.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: أَنْ and what follows it stand in place of two objects. قُلْ بَلى وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ: from your graves. ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِما عَمِلْتُمْ: that is, you will be informed of it and called to account for it. وَذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ: that is, easy, because nothing is beyond Him.
