nahhas-irab:8-8.t: فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالنُّورِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْنا: that is, the Qur'an. وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ: what governs "yawma" is "latunabbaʾunna". The pronoun in "yajmaʿukum" refers back to the name of Allah; it may not refer back to "the day": if you said "jiʾtu yawma yuwāfiquka" (I came on the day it suits you), it would not be permissible — "yawm" is not put in construct with a verb containing a pronoun referring back to it — for a reason that this is not the place to mention. ذلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); outside the Qur'an, "yawma" in the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) would be permissible. وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَيَعْمَلْ صالِحاً: conjoined (maʿṭūf); "wa-yaʿmalu" in the nominative would be permissible, as being in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئاتِهِ: that is, We erase his evil deeds from him. وَيُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها: accusative as a ḥāl. أَبَداً: as an adverb (ẓarf). ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; and "al-fawz" is salvation.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا: that is, Our proofs and arguments, and [some say] Our Book. وَالَّذِينَ: nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject). أُولئِكَ: a second mubtadaʾ. أَصْحابُ النَّارِ: the khabar (predicate) of the second, and the clause is the khabar of "alladhīna". خالِدِينَ فِيها: as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ: "al-maṣīr" is nominative by "biʾsa"; their destination is the Fire.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: "mā" here is negation and has no grammatical position. وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ: ʿIkrima read يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ with fatḥa on the dāl and "qalbuhu" in the nominative, on the basis that its origin is "yahdaʾ qalbuhu", i.e. "is set at rest"; the hamza was replaced by an alif, which was then dropped for the jussive, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 494-
سريعا وإلّا يبد بالظّلم يظلم
(Swiftly; and if he does not start the wrongdoing, he is wronged.)
وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ: that is, of what has been and of what will be.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ: that is, in what He has commanded you and forbidden you. الرَّسُولَ: conjoined. فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ: that is, if you turn your backs, are too proud to obey him and disobey him. فَإِنَّما عَلى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ: that is, [his duty is only] to convey, while the reckoning and the punishment belong to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: that is, divinity befits none but Him. وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: a command; the original form is with kasra on the lām.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: عَدُوًّا: the noun (ism) of "inna"; and "ʿaduww" may have the meaning of "aʿdāʾ" (enemies). It has been said: that is, they command you to sins and forbid you obedience, and this is the severest enmity. فَاحْذَرُوهُمْ: that is, [beware] of accepting from them. وَإِنْ تَعْفُوا: the nūn was dropped for the jussive. وَتَصْفَحُوا: conjoined to it, and likewise وَتَغْفِرُوا; that is: if you pardon what they did in the past, overlook punishing them and forgive their sins apart from that. فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ: that is, [forgiving] to whoever repents; "merciful", i.e. [He does not] punish him after repentance. [Translator's note: the text reads «رحيم أي يعذبه بعد التوبة» "merciful, i.e. He punishes him after repentance"; a negation (لا) appears to have dropped out, and it is rendered here with the negation supplied in brackets.]

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
َّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ [Translator's note: so in the text, beginning with a broken «َّما»; the verse begins إِنَّما.]
Qatāda said: that is, a trial. Ibn Zayd reported from his father, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was giving a sermon when he saw al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn stumbling along, so he came down from the pulpit, held them close to him and recited نَّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ [Translator's note: so in the text, again with the beginning of إِنَّما broken.]
Qatāda said: اللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ:
that is, Paradise.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ: «ما» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), i.e. "so fear Allah to the extent of what you are able", i.e. to the extent of your ability, like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. Qatāda's view that this verse abrogates His saying, Mighty and Majestic: اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ [Āl ʿImrān: 102] is a view that is not sound; abrogating and abrogated (al-nāsikh wa-l-mansūkh) are established only by authoritative instruction (tawqīf) or by establishing a decisive proof. The two verses agree, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not impose what is beyond ability. So the meaning of "fear Allah as He should be feared" is: in what you are able. وَاسْمَعُوا: that is, what you are commanded. وَأَطِيعُوا وَأَنْفِقُوا خَيْراً لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ: concerning the accusative of «خيرا» there are four views. The view of Sībawayh is that the meaning is "and bring about good for yourselves". It has been said: the meaning is "it will be good for yourselves". The third view: "a spending that is good for yourselves". The fourth view is that you put "khayran" in the accusative by "anfiqū" (spend), "al-khayr" being wealth. وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ: al-Farrāʾ reported that it was read "wa-man yūqa shiḥḥa nafsihi" with kasra on the shīn, and this is anomalous (shādhdh).
فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ: that is, those who have attained what they sought.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: إِنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً: that is, by your spending in His way. يُضاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ: the apodosis (mujāzāh). وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ: conjoined; it may be nominative by being cut off from the first, and accusative by "al-ṣarf" (deflection). وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ: that is, He thanks whoever spends in His way, and the meaning of His thanking him is His rewarding him and accepting his deed. حَلِيمٌ: in refraining from punishment in this world.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: It is possible that الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ is a naʿt (adjective) of the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that "ʿālimu al-ghayb" is a second khabar (predicate), or a naʿt if it has the sense of the past, because it is then definite. It is also possible that all of it is a badal (substitute), because a definite may be substituted for an indefinite.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {لَهُ الملك}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. He put the khabar first to give the sense of the restriction of dominion and praise to Allah, since dominion and praise belong to Allah in reality.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {صُوَرَكُمْ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the ṣād, which is the regular form for fuʿla. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Aʿmash and Abū Zayd read it with kasra, which is not regular, and it is the reverse of «لُحَى» with ḍamma, where the regular form is «لِحى» with kasra.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ}: the majority read both words in the second person. It is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim with the yāʾ of the third person, which allows for an iltifāt (shift of person) and allows for informing about those absent.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {بِأَنَّهُ}: the hāʾ is the pronoun of the matter and the account (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and {كَانَت تَّأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُم} is its khabar. «استغنى» is in the sense of the bare verb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "His self-sufficiency became manifest; so the sīn is not for requesting."
His saying: {أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنَا}: it may be nominative as agent, being a case of ishtighāl (preoccupation), which is the preferred, because the particle seeks a verb; or it may be a mubtadaʾ and khabar. The pronoun in «يَهْدوننا» was put in the plural because «البشر» is a generic noun.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {أَن لَّن يُبْعَثُواْ}: «أنْ» is the lightened one, not the subjunctive, so that a subjunctive particle does not enter upon its like; and «أنْ» with what is in its sphere stands in the place of the two objects of "claiming", or of the one object. «بلى» is an affirmation of the negation, and «لَتُبْعَثُنَّ» is the answer to an implied oath.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ}: accusative by His saying «لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ» in the view of al-Naḥḥās, by «خَبيرٌ» in the view of al-Ḥawfī, and by an implied «اذكُر» in the view of al-Zamakhsharī, in which case it is a direct object; and by what the speech points to, that is, "you will differ in rank on the day He gathers you", Abū l-Baqāʾ said. The majority read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the ʿayn. Quiescence of it and ishmām are transmitted from Abū ʿAmr. This is reported from him for the rāʾ, for example {يَنصُرُكُمْ} [al-Mulk: 20] and its like, as was given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara. Yaʿqūb, Sallām, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and al-Shaʿbī read «نجمعكم» with the nūn of magnification.
التَّغابُن is a tafāʿul from الغَبْن in buying and selling, used metaphorically, and it is taking a thing for less than its value. It was also said: الغَبْن is concealment, and from it comes غَبْنُ البيعِ, because of its being hidden. The tafāʿul here is from one party and not from two. One says: غَبَنْتُ الثوبَ and خَبَنْتُه, that is, I took what was longer than your measure of it, so it is a diminishing and a concealing. In the exegesis: it is that a man earns wealth by illegitimate means, and another inherits it and uses it in obedience to Allah, so that the first enters the Fire and the second the Garden through that wealth; that is the manifest loss (al-ghabn al-mubīn).

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ}: with a yāʾ, jussive, as the apodosis of the condition, is the reading of the majority. Ibn Jubayr, Ibn Hurmuz, Ṭalḥa and al-Azraq read it with a nūn; al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «يُهْدَ» in the passive, «قلبُه» taking the place of the agent. Mālik ibn Dīnār and ʿAmr ibn Dīnār read «يَهْدَأْ» with a quiescent hamza, «قلبُه» being the agent of it, in the sense of being at rest and still. ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read «يَهْدا» with an alif substituted for the hamza, like the one before it, and did not drop it, having regard to the original; and it is the more eloquent of the two dialects. ʿIkrima and Mālik ibn Dīnār also read يَهْدَ with this alif dropped, treating it like an original alif, as in the saying of Zuhayr:
4270 - جَريءٌ متى يُظْلَمْ يُعاقِبْ بِظُلْمِه ... سريعاً وإنْ لا يُبْدَ بالظلمِ يُظْلَمِ
(Bold: when wronged he repays his wrong swiftly, and if he is not begun with wrong, he is wronged.) [Translator's note: the final verb is printed in the passive, «يُظْلَمِ», as in the source; the usual transmission of this verse has the active «يَظْلِمِ», "he does wrong".]
The i'rāb of what precedes this verse and what follows it has already been given.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {خَيْراً لأَنفُسِكُمْ}: there are several possibilities. The first, which is the saying of Sībawayh, is that it is a direct object of an implied verb, that is: "and bring good", as in His saying {انتهوا خَيْراً لَّكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 171]. The second: its implied form is "let the spending be good", so it is the khabar of an implied kāna; this is the saying of Abū ʿUbayd. The third is that it is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, which is the saying of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, that is: "a good spending". The fourth is that it is a ḥāl, which is the saying of the Kufans. The fifth is that it is an object of His saying «أَنْفِقوا», that is: "spend good wealth". The disagreement about the reading of {يُضَاعِفَهُ} [al-Ḥadīd: 11] and {يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ} [al-Ḥashr: 9] has already been given.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا أَصَابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ. . . (١١))
His saying (يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ) is also read with a hamza [يَهْدَأْ قَلْبُهُ], i.e. "his heart will be at rest".

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ وَاسْمَعُوا وَأَطِيعُوا وَأَنْفِقُوا خَيْرًا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (١٦))
His saying (خَيْرًا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ): it is like His saying (انْتَهُوا خَيْرًا لَكُمْ). And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُ كَانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَقَالُوا أَبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنَا فَكَفَرُوا وَتَوَلَّوْا وَاسْتَغْنَى اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ (٦))
His saying (أَبَشَرٌ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «يَهْدُونَنَا» is the khabar (predicate); it may also be a fāʿil (agent) [of an implied verb], i.e. "shall a human being guide us?"

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ لِيَوْمِ الْجَمْعِ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغَابُنِ. . . (٩))
His saying (يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكُمْ): it is an adverb (ẓarf) for خَبِيرٍ.
It is also said: for what the context indicates, i.e. "you will differ [in rank] on the day He gathers you".
It is also said: the implied form is "remember the day He gathers you".

zajjaj:2-2.t:
Sūrat al-Taghābun (Mutual Loss and Gain)
﷽
Makkan, except for three verses that were revealed in Medina, and they are at its end: His saying ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنَّ مِن أزْواجِكُمْ﴾ [al-Taghābun: 14] to its end. And it is said that the correct view is that it is entirely Medinan.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكم فَمِنكم كافِرٌ ومِنكم مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ — He created you in your mothers' wombs as disbelievers and believers. It has come in the exegesis that Yaḥyā (peace be upon him) was created a believer in his mother's womb, and Pharaoh was created a disbeliever in his mother's womb. The proof of what is in the exegesis is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَنادَتْهُ المَلائِكَةُ وهو قائِمٌ يُصَلِّي في المِحْرابِ أنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيى مُصَدِّقًا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وسَيِّدًا وحَصُورًا ونَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 39]; so Allah the Exalted made known that he was created thus. It is also possible that ﴿خَلَقَكم فَمِنكم كافِرٌ ومِنكم مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ means: one who believes that Allah created him, and one who disbelieves that Allah created him. The proof of that is His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿قُتِلَ الإنْسانُ ما أكْفَرَهُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 17] ﴿مِن أيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 18] ﴿مِن نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 19], and He said: ﴿أكَفَرْتَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ سَوّاكَ رَجُلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 37].

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿وَصَوَّرَكم فَأحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ﴾ — it is also read ”صِوَرَكُمْ“ with a kasra on the ṣād. ”صُورَةٌ“ has the plural ”صُوَرٌ“, like ”غُرْفَةٌ“ / ”غُرَفٌ“ and ”رُشْوَةٌ“ / ”رُشًى“; and it also has the plural ”صِوَرٌ“, like ”رِشْوَةٌ“ / ”رِشًى“. ”فُعَلٌ“ and ”فِعَلٌ“ are sisters: they said ”حُلًى“ and ”حِلًى“, and ”لِحًى“ and ”لُحًى“, the plural of ”لِحَيَّةٌ“ [Translator's note: so vowelled in the text; the word is لِحْيَة, beard]. The meaning of ”أحْسَنَ صُوَرَكم“ is: He created you the finest of all living creatures. The proof of that is that a human being would not be pleased for his form to be other than the form of the children of Ādam; so man is the finest of living creatures. It is also said that ”فَأحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ“ means: whomever Allah willed to be white was white, whomever He willed to be black was black, whomever He willed to be ill-favoured was ill-favoured, or well-formed was well-formed; so He, Mighty and Majestic, made that excellent and brought forth from every form every kind according to His will.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿ألَمْ يَأْتِكم نَبَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن قَبْلُ فَذاقُوا وبالَ أمْرِهِمْ ولَهم عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾ means: they tasted in this world mighty assaults, and in the Hereafter they will have a painful punishment. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known why that befell them, and said: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهُ كانَتْ تَأْتِيهِمْ رُسُلُهم بِالبَيِّناتِ فَقالُوا أبَشَرٌ يَهْدُونَنا فَكَفَرُوا وتَوَلَّوْا﴾ [al-Taghābun: 6]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the punishment befell them in this world, and that it will befall them in the Hereafter, because of their disbelief.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ والنُّورِ الَّذِي أنْـزَلْنا﴾ means: and in the Quran, which is a light and a clear Book.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكم لِيَوْمِ الجَمْعِ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ﴾ — ”يَوْمَ“ is accusative through His saying "لَتُبْعَثُنَّ ثُمَّ لَتُنَبَّؤُنَّ بِما عَمِلْتُمْ يَوْمَ الجَمْعِ" [Translator's note: so quoted; the words يوم الجمع are not part of verse 7 in the muṣḥaf]. ”يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ“ is the day when the people of Paradise get the better of (yaghbinu) the people of the Fire, and the one whose rank in Paradise is raised gets the better of whoever is below his rank. That is struck as a likeness of buying and selling, as He said: ﴿هَلْ أدُلُّكم عَلى تِجارَةٍ تُنْجِيكم مِن عَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 10] ﴿تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 11], and He said in another place: ﴿فَما رَبِحَتْ تِجارَتُهم وما كانُوا مُهْتَدِينَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 16], and that concerns those who bought error in exchange for guidance.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿ما أصابَ مِن مُصِيبَةٍ إلا بِإذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ means: except by the command of Allah; and it is also said: except by the knowledge of Allah.

His saying: ﴿وَمَن يُؤْمِن بِاللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ﴾ — and submits, at the time of the calamity, to the command of Allah, He guides his heart, i.e. He makes it rightly guided. It was also read ”يَهْدَ قَلْبُهُ“, interpreted from ”هَدَأ قَلْبُهُ، يَهْدَأُ“ (his heart became calm), when it becomes still; it would then be with the hamza dropped, so that in the indicative it would be ”يَهْدا قَلْبُهُ“ without hamza, and in the jussive ”مَن يُؤْمِن بِاللَّهِ يَهْدَ قَلْبُهُ“, with the alif dropped for the jussive. The interpretation would then be: "when he submits to the command of Allah, his heart becomes calm."

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ مِن أزْواجِكم وأوْلادِكم عَدُوًّا لَكم فاحْذَرُوهُمْ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that when the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to emigrate from Makka to Medina, some people wished to emigrate, and their wives and children said to them: "We have borne with you your leaving the religion, but we will not bear with you your leaving us and leaving the property and the dwellings." So Allah the Exalted made known that whoever is in this condition is an enemy, even if it be a child or a wife. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, commanded pardon and overlooking, and said: ﴿وَإنْ تَعْفُوا وتَصْفَحُوا وتَغْفِرُوا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾. Then He made known that wealth and children are among the things by which one is tried, and said: ﴿إنَّما أمْوالُكم وأوْلادُكم فِتْنَةٌ واللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ أجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ [al-Taghābun: 15].

﴿فاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ما اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ [al-Taghābun: 16] means: as far as jihad and emigration with the Prophet ﷺ are possible for you; so let not inclination towards wealth and children seduce you away from that.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿فاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ما اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ — this is a concession with respect to His saying: ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 102].

His saying: ﴿وَأنْفِقُوا خَيْرًا لأنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ means: send forth good for yourselves from your wealth. ﴿وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ﴾ — ”وَمَن يُوَقَّ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ“ is also permissible, but I know of no one who read it, so do not recite it unless a transmission of its recitation is established. ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ﴾ means: those who attain triumph and good.

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿إنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا يُضاعِفْهُ لَكم ويَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾ — so He, Mighty and Majestic, asked for a loan from what He Himself provided and gave, as a favour and a test. ﴿واللَّهُ شَكُورٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾: He appreciates (yashkuru) what you have done, and is forbearing with you when you deserve punishment for your sins.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿عالِمُ الغَيْبِ والشَّهادَةِ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾ — He knows what the breasts conceal, of what the guardian angels do not know, and He knows every leaf that falls and every drop of rain that drips.
